blind_audit.rationale: TAP is a heterodimer composed of TAP1 and TAP2 that uses ATP to move cytosolic peptides into the endoplasmic reticulum. These peptides are loaded onto nascent MHC class I molecules before surface expression. TAP2 loss therefore reduces peptide-loaded MHC class I at the cell surface and is associated with selective CD8+ T-cell lymphopenia.

nearest_material_review.tested_construct: CIITA and the RFX complex are transcriptional regulators required for MHC class II gene expression. Loss of CIITA can abolish MHC II expression on antigen-presenting cells, impairing positive selection and peripheral activation of CD4-positive T cells and causing combined immunodeficiency.
